briefdescription.para: XAxiEthernet_Start starts the Axi Ethernet device as follows:.

para.verbatim: - Enable transmitter if XAE_TRANSMIT_ENABLE_OPTION is set - Enable receiver if XAE_RECEIVER_ENABLE_OPTION is set

parameterdescription.para: is a pointer to the Axi Ethernet instance to be worked on.

briefdescription.para: XAxiEthernet_Stop gracefully stops the Axi Ethernet device as follows:.

para.verbatim: - Disable all interrupts from this device - Disable the receiver

detaileddescription.para: XAxiEthernet_Stop does not modify any of the current device options.
Since the transmitter is not disabled, frames currently in internal buffers or in process by a DMA engine are allowed to be transmitted.

parameterdescription.para: is a pointer to the Axi Ethernet instance to be worked on.

briefdescription.para: XAxiEthernet_Reset does not perform a soft reset of the AxiEthernet core.

detaileddescription.para: AxiEthernet hardware is reset by the device connected to the AXI4-Stream interface. Inserts some delay before proceeding to check for MgtRdy bit. The delay is necessary to be at a safe side. It takes a while for the reset process to complete and for any of the AxiEthernet registers to be accessed. It then checks for MgtRdy bit in IS register to know if AxiEthernet reset is completed or not. Subsequently it calls one more driver function to complete the AxiEthernet hardware initialization.

parameterdescription.para: is a pointer to the Axi Ethernet instance to be worked on.

simplesect.para: It is the responsibility of the user to reset the AxiEthernet hardware before using it. AxiEthernet hardware should be reset through the device connected to the AXI4-Stream interface of AxiEthernet.

briefdescription.para: Checks and updates dependent options for new or extended features.

detaileddescription.para: This helper function is called from XAxiEthernet_SetOptions() and XAxiEthernet_ClearOptions().

InstancePtr
is a pointer to the Axi Ethernet instance to be worked on.
Dependent options that are required to set/clear per hardware requirement. This helper function collects the dependent OPTION(s) per hardware design. When conflicts arises, extended features have precedence over legacy ones. Two operations to be considered,
Adding extended options. If XATE_VLAN_OPTION is enabled and enable one of extended VLAN options, XATE_VLAN_OPTION should be off and configure to hardware. However, axi-ethernet instance Options variable still holds XATE_VLAN_OPTION so when all of the extended feature are removed, XATE_VLAN_OPTION can be effective and configured to hardware.
Removing extended options. Remove extended option can not just remove the selected extended option and dependent options. All extended options need to be verified and remained when one or more extended options are enabled.

Dependent options are :
XAE_VLAN_OPTION,
XAE_JUMBO_OPTION
XAE_FCS_INSERT_OPTION,
XAE_FCS_STRIP_OPTION
XAE_PROMISC_OPTION.

briefdescription.para: XAxiEthernet_PhyRead reads the specified PHY register, RegiseterNum.

detaileddescription.para: on the PHY specified by PhyAddress into PhyDataPtr. This Ethernet driver does not require the device to be stopped before reading from the PHY. It is the responsibility of the calling code to stop the device if it is deemed necessary.
Note that the Axi Ethernet hardware provides the ability to talk to a PHY that adheres to the Media Independent Interface (MII) as defined in the IEEE 802.3 standard.

para.bold: It is important that calling code set up the MDIO clock with XAxiEthernet_PhySetMdioDivisor() prior to accessing the PHY with this function.

detaileddescription.para:
InstancePtr
is a pointer to the Axi Ethernet instance to be worked on.
PhyAddress
is the address of the PHY to be written (multiple PHYs supported).
RegisterNum
is the register number, 0-31, of the specific PHY register to write.
PhyDataPtr
is a reference to the location where the 16-bit result value is stored.
There is the possibility that this function will not return if the hardware is broken (i.e., it never sets the status bit indicating that the write is done). If this is of concern, the calling code should provide a mechanism suitable for recovery.

memberdef.name: XAxiEthernet_PhyWrite

briefdescription.para: XAxiEthernet_PhyWrite writes PhyData to the specified PHY register, RegiseterNum on the PHY specified by PhyAddress.

detaileddescription.para: This Ethernet driver does not require the device to be stopped before writing to the PHY. It is the responsibility of the calling code to stop the device if it is deemed necessary.
Note that the Axi Ethernet hardware provides the ability to talk to a PHY that adheres to the Media Independent Interface (MII) as defined in the IEEE 802.3 standard.

para.bold: It is important that calling code set up the MDIO clock with XAxiEthernet_PhySetMdioDivisor() prior to accessing the PHY with this function.

detaileddescription.para:
InstancePtr
is a pointer to the Axi Ethernet instance to be worked on.
PhyAddress
is the address of the PHY to be written (multiple PHYs supported).
RegisterNum
is the register number, 0-31, of the specific PHY register to write.
PhyData
is the 16-bit value that will be written to the register.
There is the possibility that this function will not return if the hardware is broken (i.e., it never sets the status bit indicating that the write is done). If this is of concern, the calling code should provide a mechanism suitable for recovery.
